import cookie helpers.description: Server-side cookie helper for Framework mode.

createCookie().description: A signed, typed cookie. Parse with `await cookie.parse(request.headers.get('Cookie'))`, write with `await cookie.serialize(value)`.

cookie parse / serialize.description: Read a cookie in a loader and write it back on the response.

import createCookieSessionStorage.description: Session storage backed by a cookie.

body: export const { getSession, commitSession, destroySession } = createCookieSessionStorage({
createCookieSessionStorage().description:
The usual session setup: the whole session lives in a signed cookie, so no server store is needed.
Size is capped at ~4kb — keep only ids in it.

session read / commit.description:
Read a session in a loader/action and persist any changes with `commitSession`.
Every mutation needs the `Set-Cookie` header, or the change is lost.

session flash message.description:
A value read exactly once, then removed — the standard post-redirect toast.
Read it with `session.get('message')` in the next loader.

body: export const { getSession, commitSession, destroySession } = createMemorySessionStorage({
createMemorySessionStorage().description: Keeps sessions in memory. For tests and local development only — everything is lost on restart, and it does not survive multiple processes.

body: export const { getSession, commitSession, destroySession } = createSessionStorage({
createSessionStorage().description:
Custom-backed sessions — the cookie holds only an id, the data lives in your store (DB, Redis, KV).
Use this when sessions exceed the cookie size limit or must be revocable server-side.

isCookie() / isSession().description: Type guards for the cookie and session objects. Mostly useful inside libraries and adapters.
